messages:
sara-sales: Hey team, customer POC is failing intermittently when they send a single document set (~1.2MB) to our embeddings endpoint. No 413 from their proxy, but result is truncated mid-sentence. They say it used to work with another vendor.

eli-eng: Can you paste the raw request headers + body size they send? Might be a charset / content-length mismatch.

sara-sales: Here’s what they pasted from their env: 
```
POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-16
Content-Length: 1203456

{... huge JSON payload ...}
```
They told me they were testing with a legacy Java service that emits UTF-16 by default.

kevin-ml: UTF-16 will double the byte count for ascii text; our server assumes UTF-8 and does token estimation on byte length. If their Content-Length reflects UTF-16 bytes but we decode as UTF-8 it could be truncating tokens.

maya-se: Also our request size limiter is currently enforced on bytes after we decode body to UTF-8. If the header reports X but payload is different encoding, the streaming parser may cut the body earlier.

eli-eng: Can you ask them to resend as `charset=utf-8` or remove the charset header? Quick repro: set `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-16` and we see `Invalid continuation byte` in parser logs.

sara-sales: They attached a sample. I uploaded to the shared bucket: https://redwood.test/poc-samples/4332.

infra-bot: deploy-log: parsing error at bytes=65536, handler=request-body-limiter, code=PAYLOAD_TRUNCATED

kevin-ml: That log shows we hit our 64KB streaming chunk and flagged truncation. If the client says 1.2MB but we see invalid UTF-8 sequences while reading, the parser will stop and treat remainder as truncated.

maya-se: Short-term workaround: ask them to UTF-8 encode payload or gzip the JSON body and set `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Our edge will accept gzipped bodies (we decompress before limit checks).

eli-eng: Another option: multipart upload of chunks + server-side concat (we support multipart with presigned URLs). For embeddings, chunking by semantic segments is better anyway.

liz-shipit: Pricing note for sales: if they switch to chunking + multiple embedding calls we should estimate additional cost and throughput. I can spin up a quick TCO calc once we know average chunk size.

kevin-ml: Also tell them to avoid sending UTF-16 BOM; some clients embed BOM which breaks some JSON parsers. Example bad prefix: `FF FE` at start.

maya-se: Quick debugging instructions to give the customer: 
1) Confirm `Content-Type` charset is `utf-8` or omit charset.
2) Ensure body bytes actually match Content-Length (use `curl -v --data-binary @file`).
3) Try `Content-Encoding: gzip` + compressed body.
4) Or split doc into <= 256k chunks and call embeddings in parallel.

sara-sales: I sent the workaround steps and asked them to repro. Customer replied they can re-encode and test tomorrow morning. They asked if we can temporarily relax server-side truncation for their org.

eli-eng: We can't change global limits for now. For Dedicated customers we can change policy on a per-tenant basis, but this POC is hosted. We can offer a short-term internal proxy to re-encode for them if they grant debug logs.

kevin-ml: If they need exact cross-vendor parity, remind them different vendors have different decoding behaviors; best is to normalize to UTF-8 and use deterministic chunking.

maya-se: If they come back still failing, ask for a small reproducible curl command + exact bytes (safest is a redacted file) so we can run it through the same edge.

sara-sales: Thanks — will follow up after their test. If it fails i'll open a swarming thread with a repro. :raised_hands:
